note: CRM field extraction from one English call transcript. Same 32 inputs and the same train/heldout split as evals/transcript-en (the summary exam); only the expected block differs. Eight fields, each a verbatim token from the transcript or the literal string 'not stated'. Field-level scoring: partial credit per field, a case passes only if all eight match (case-insensitive exact string). 'not stated' is a literal expected VALUE, so an output that omits a key earns nothing for it (the fields scorer reads a missing key as null, which would otherwise pass a null expectation for free -- evals/test_call_fields.py pins this). Labels were written by hand from the transcripts on 2026-09-25 under the rules in agents/call-fields/prompt.md; every non-null label is a case-insensitive substring of its transcript (guard in evals/test_call_fields.py, seen red).
not_verified: Exact-string matching means a value that is correct but written differently counts as wrong with no credit: '15th' for 'the fifteenth', 'end of day' for 'today', '1,500' for '1500'. The amount rule (final agreed amount; else the option the customer preferred; else the recurring plan price) and the next_step_date rule (agreed call or meeting; else the date one side promised to get back; else the earliest deliverable date) are stated in the prompt, but a call with several candidate amounts or dates is graded against ONE hand-picked label, so a defensible alternative reading scores zero on that field -- known instances: renewal-heldout-medium (950 vs 684/836), discovery-long-train (800 pilot vs 3200 plan), discovery-heldout-long (Idris vs Meredith as decision maker), longcall-renewal-train-1 (next Wednesday, the budget-approval date, vs Friday, the seat-count date), longcall-discovery-train-1 (next week, the agreed technical call, vs Thursday, the quote deadline), discovery-heldout-long (today, the earliest deliverable, because the agreed readout 'at the end of the 30-day pilot' carries no day or date token -- tier (a) needs one; correctness refuter, 25 Sep). Vendor-name-as-company: renewal-medium-train ('your current contract with Solvix') and renewal-heldout-medium ('your Vantable contract') are labelled company='not stated' because the name is the REP's product, not the customer's firm; 6 of 9 hosted models wrote the vendor name. The first train pass (25 Sep, gemma4-e4b-ctx16k, 9/13) missed exactly these two date calls plus two rule-literal errors (a role instead of a name; an unnamed 'competitor's tool'); the prompt was clarified on those rules and no label was changed. It does not check that the eight fields are the right schema for any real CRM, and it cannot grade money written in European notation (no decimal-comma normalisation exists; CLAUDE.md gotcha 4). All 32 transcripts are synthetic; the 10 longcall-* transcripts are a short opening plus one repeated filler block plus a substantive tail. competitor is 'not stated' in every one of the 32 cases, both splits: no transcript names a rival vendor (one mentions an unnamed 'competitor's tool'), so the field is ABSTENTION-ONLY -- it catches an invented competitor and nothing else; an agent that hardcodes 'not stated' for it is never caught. A positive competitor case needs a new committed transcript.

REP: Hi, this is Tom from support, I understand you've been having trouble
with the export feature — can you walk me through what's happening?

and since last Tuesday every CSV export from the patient scheduling module
comes back with the appointment times shifted by an hour. It's causing real
problems because our front desk staff are double-booking slots.
REP: That sounds disruptive, I'm sorry. Let me make sure I understand the
scope — is this every export, or only certain reports?
CUSTOMER: It's specifically the daily schedule export, the one our office
managers run every morning at 7am. The weekly summary export looks fine as
far as we can tell.
REP: Okay, that's a useful distinction. Do you know if this started right
after an update on your end, or did it just appear on its own?
CUSTOMER: We didn't change anything. Our IT lead, Grace, thinks it might be
related to daylight saving time, since the shift is exactly one hour, but
she's not certain.
REP: That's a strong lead actually — a timezone handling bug around a DST
boundary would produce exactly a one-hour shift on exports but leave the
in-app calendar correct, which matches what you're describing. Can you
confirm — does the calendar view inside the app show the correct times?
CUSTOMER: Yes, in-app everything is correct. It's only the exported file
that's wrong.
REP: Understood, that narrows it down to the export pipeline specifically,
not the underlying data. I'm going to open a ticket right now and mark it
Sev2 given the double-booking impact. Can I get your account ID to attach to
the ticket?
CUSTOMER: It's LC-40217.
REP: Got it, LC-40217. I'll also need one example export file if you can
send it, so engineering can see the exact offset in your data.
CUSTOMER: I can send this morning's export. Should I email it to this
address?
REP: Yes, support@ourcompany.example works, please put LC-40217 in the
subject line so it routes straight to this ticket.
CUSTOMER: Will do, sending it right after this call.
REP: Thank you. Now, while engineering investigates, is there a workaround
your team can use in the meantime? For example, manually adjusting the
export time before printing the schedule?
CUSTOMER: We've actually started doing that already — Grace wrote a note
telling the front desk to subtract an hour from every exported time until
this is fixed, but it's error-prone and everyone's stressed about missing
one.
REP: That's a reasonable stopgap but I agree it's risky at scale. Let me
check something — do you use the export as a PDF anywhere, or is it always
CSV?
CUSTOMER: Always CSV, we pipe it into our own printer template.
REP: Okay. I don't have a faster fix to offer you on this call, but I want
to set clear expectations rather than guess. Engineering triages Sev2
tickets within 4 business hours, and depending on what they find, a timezone
bug like this is usually a same-day or next-day fix once identified, but I
can't promise a number until they've looked at the actual code path.
CUSTOMER: I understand, I'd just like to know when I'll hear something next,
even if it's not resolved yet.
REP: Fair. I'll personally follow up with you by end of day tomorrow with a
status update, whether or not it's fixed by then. If it looks like it will
take longer, I'll escalate again on your behalf.
CUSTOMER: That would help a lot, thank you. Also — will we get any credit
for this given the front desk overhead it's causing?
REP: I can't approve a credit myself, but I will flag it to our account
team, and typically a service issue causing operational impact like this
does get reviewed for a service credit. I don't want to promise a number
since that's not my call to make.
CUSTOMER: That's fair, I just wanted it noted somewhere.
REP: Understood, I'm noting it in the ticket now so the account team sees it
when they review.
CUSTOMER: Appreciated. One more thing while I have you — separately from
this bug, we've been wanting to ask about adding a second location. We're
opening a clinic in Riverside next month and want to know if that's a
straightforward add to our existing plan or a new contract.
REP: That's outside what I handle day to day, but I can connect you with
your account manager, Felix, for that conversation — he'll know your
current plan terms. Should I have him reach out, or would you rather book
time directly?
CUSTOMER: Having him reach out is fine, no rush on that one, the export bug
is the priority today.
REP: Understood, I'll message Felix after this call and mention Riverside so
he has context whenever you're ready to talk.
CUSTOMER: Great, thank you.
REP: To make sure I've got everything — I'm opening a Sev2 ticket for
LC-40217 on the daily schedule export DST offset, you'll send an example
CSV to support@ourcompany.example with LC-40217 in the subject, I'll follow
up by end of day tomorrow with a status update regardless of resolution, I'm
flagging the operational impact for a possible service credit review, and
I'll message Felix to reach out about the Riverside second location.
CUSTOMER: That all matches what we discussed. Thank you for being thorough.
REP: Of course. Is there anything else I can help with today?
CUSTOMER: No, that covers everything on my end.
REP: Great, talk to you tomorrow, Grace — I mean, talk to you tomorrow, and
please tell Grace thanks for the DST theory, that's probably going to save
engineering some time.
CUSTOMER: Ha, I will. Thanks Tom.
REP: Before you go, actually — while I have the ticket open, can you tell me
roughly what time zone your clinic is in? It'll save engineering a step.
CUSTOMER: We're in Eastern time, same as most of our sister clinics except
the Denver one, which is Mountain.
REP: That's helpful, I'll note both time zones on the ticket in case the bug
behaves differently across them — sometimes a DST bug only shows up in
regions that observe it a certain way, so it's worth ruling in or out early.
CUSTOMER: Good thinking. Should I ask the Denver office to send an export
too, or is Larkspur's enough for now?
REP: If it's not too much trouble, yes — a second example from a different
time zone would genuinely help engineering confirm the pattern faster rather
than guessing from one data point.
CUSTOMER: I'll reach out to the Denver office manager today and have them
send an export to the same address with LC-40217 in the subject.
REP: Perfect, that's a real help, thank you. I'm updating the ticket now to
note that a second export from the Denver, Mountain-time location is
expected as well.
CUSTOMER: Sounds good. Is there a ticket number I can reference if I need to
call back before tomorrow?
REP: Yes, it's the same LC-40217, that's both your account ID and the
ticket reference, so any agent who picks it up will see the full history.
CUSTOMER: Great, that makes it easy. I think that's really everything now.
REP: One last thing on my end — I noticed your plan is still on the legacy
scheduling module version. That's not related to this bug, but the legacy
version is being retired at the end of next quarter, so at some point you'll
need to migrate. I don't want to push that today given everything else
going on, but I'll have Felix mention it when he reaches out about
Riverside, so it's on your radar rather than a surprise later.
CUSTOMER: Appreciate the heads up, better to know now than get caught off
guard later.
REP: Agreed. Alright, I think we've covered everything — Sev2 ticket
LC-40217 open for the DST export offset, example CSVs coming from both
Larkspur and the Denver office, my status update tomorrow by end of day, the
service credit flag for the account team, Felix reaching out about
Riverside and mentioning the legacy module retirement. Anything I've missed?
CUSTOMER: No, I think that's a complete list, thank you for being so
thorough on this call.
REP: Happy to help, talk tomorrow.
CUSTOMER: Ha, I will. Thanks Tom.
REP: Take care.

weekly.

mean absolute percentage error, which is roughly where a manual spreadsheet

improving after that as the model sees more of your actual pattern.
PROSPECT: That would be a big improvement for us — right now we're
overstocking about 22% of SKUs and stocking out on another 9%, mostly
because Devon can't realistically track seasonality for 1400 items by hand.
REP: Those numbers line up with what we typically see going in. On pricing,

PROSPECT: Okay, I think I have what I need to bring this to our VP of

REP: That's great. Would it help if I sent a short summary document you

PROSPECT: Yes please, that would save me writing it up myself.
